STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit) -> u3
(u0, siren_ringing & !at_exit) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, at_exit) -> u3
(u1, switch_toggled & !at_exit) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, at_exit) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u1, switch_toggled & !at_exit, u2) -> 0.1
(u0, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
(u1, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
(u2, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: Accepted. Format: all required headers (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION) are present in the paper format; FINAL_STATES is nonempty (u3), u3 is declared in STATES, is reachable, and is the accepting state entered exactly on the exit transition, kept absorbing by an else self-loop. Semantic fidelity: the task is 'reach the exit' (primary) with a soft preference 'if the siren sounds, toggle the switch at least once'. The RM encodes u0 (siren not yet sounded) -> u1 on the first step siren_ringing is true (persistent condition, so it fires once at onset; onset and at_exit cannot coincide since the siren cannot start on the last step), u1 -> u2 on switch_toggled with a one-time 0.1 bonus, and at_exit -> u3 with 1.0 from u0, u1 and u2. Since the siren stops only via a toggle, any toggle while in u1 necessarily silences a ringing siren, so the 0.1 always corresponds to actually responding to the siren. Exiting while the siren still rings still pays 1.0, which faithfully matches the soft 'preferably' phrasing; conditioning the exit reward on u2 would wrongly make the preference hard and would leave no-siren setups unable to reach the goal reward. Reward safety: only non-negative rewards; the bonus is paid exactly once (no u2->u1 edge, so re-rings and re-toggles in u2 earn nothing), total is bounded at 1.1, and the bonus (0.1) is below the goal reward (1.0), so exiting always dominates toggling without exiting, while toggling-then-exiting dominates exiting directly in siren setups. No reward is paid for the siren onset itself, which is not agent-controlled. Coverage and ordering: every state ends with an else self-loop, so irrelevant events (holding_box, box_fell, no-op steps) are absorbed without state change; within each state the specific guards are mutually exclusive and precede the else, giving deterministic ordered coverage. The reward function is consistent with the transition function: every rewarded triple matches a declared transition and all others default to 0. Omitting the box propositions entirely is correct, since the task says nothing about the box and including them would over-specify. Regressions: none required — 'at least once' means a single toggle suffices even if the siren starts a second time, so the absence of a u2->u1 regression is right. Edge cases: if a ring falls on the same step as a toggle (action applies before due events), the step ends with siren_ringing true and the RM moves u0->u1 with no bonus, requiring a further toggle for the preference — consistent with the environment's event ordering, since that toggle could not have silenced a siren that had not yet started; a toggle while the siren is silent in u0 earns nothing, matching the preference's condition on the siren having sounded. Minor non-blocking note: the !at_exit conjuncts in (u0, siren_ringing & !at_exit) and (u1, switch_toggled & !at_exit) are redundant given the environment constraints and guard ordering, but harmless and make exclusivity explicit.

candidate:
def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing
def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step
def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"
def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step
def at_exit(env): return env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]) is not None and env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]).type == "goal"
feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented with exactly one function each, and no undeclared extras. Alignment with the documented API: siren_ringing returns env.siren_ringing as specified; switch_toggled and box_fell test membership of 'toggle'/'fall' in env.events_this_step, matching the event semantics for the step that just ended without needing previous_valuation; holding_box matches the documented expression including the None guard on env.carrying before reading .type; at_exit guards the empty cell with 'is not None' before reading .type and checks type == 'goal', equivalent to the documented grid lookup at env.agent_pos. All functions return boolean-valued expressions, are syntactically valid Python, contain no imports, no actions, and no mutations of the environment or episode memory (read-only attribute access only). No runtime or semantic errors are apparent: all accessed attributes (siren_ringing, events_this_step, carrying, agent_pos, grid.get) are in the documented labeling API, and grid coordinates come from the agent's own position so they are always in range.
